page.overview:
Who is Achilles?

When first seen, Achilles and B'kai were leading a group of Greek Soldiers in a mission to climb the walls of Troy while the rest of the army distracted the Trojans with an attack on the city gate. The group made it to the top, but the Trojans spotted them and Odysseus was forced to call for a retreat. Achilles, never one to give up, tried to continue the attack, and B'kai had to convince him the battle was lost. That night, Achilles confessed to B'kai that, like most soldiers, he began to feel the war was a lost cause, and the glory and legends he hoped to create here would be nothing but tales about Greek men dying pointless deaths. B'kai did his best to cheer Achilles up by reminding him what they were fighting for, with Achilles praising "Memnon" for his devition to the war despite not being from Greek. When a soldier named Ferro accused Memnon of being a Trojan spy, Achilles stood up for his friend and reminded Ferro that Memnon had been fighting for the Greek for nine years now and saved many of them countless times. The following day, Achilles even gave Memnon an amulet he received from his mother as a token of their friendship.

When Odysseus came up with the strategy for the Trojan Horse, Achilles and B'kai where among the soldiers hiding in the horse as it was brought into the city gates. But in the fight that followd, B'kai left Achilles to make his way to the Royal Palace. When Achilles caught up with him, he saw how B'kai allowed both Helen and Paris to escape the city (as he already took the pendant from them, and that was the only thing he wanted). Now convinced that Ferro was right and B'kai had been a spy all along, Achilles attacked his former friend. In the fight that followed, B'kai was eventually forced to deliver Achilles a fatal blow after slicing his weak spot: his heel. As Achilles lay dying, B'kai reminded him that, like Achilles himself, he had simply been fighting for his home, and assured his old friend that not everything had been a lie.

After Achilles passed away, B'kai took a moment to, per Greek tradition, put coins on both of Achilles' eyes, before returning to Wakanda.
